takeaway: Qualitative coding has four main families, each suited to a different kind of question.
explain_script: There are several ways to code qualitative data. Descriptive coding names the topic, in vivo coding keeps the participant's own words, process coding tracks action over time, and values coding captures beliefs. Researchers often combine them across passes.

nodes.label: Descriptive coding
nodes.one_line: Assigns a short noun phrase summarizing what a passage is about.

nodes.label: In vivo coding
nodes.one_line: Uses the participant's own words as the code itself.

nodes.label: Process coding
nodes.one_line: Uses action words to capture change or transition over time.

nodes.label: Values coding
nodes.one_line: Applies codes reflecting a participant's values, attitudes, and beliefs.

edges.label: preserves meaning that flattens
edges.quote: preserving the vernacular meaning that descriptive coding can flatten

edges.label: is often paired with
edges.quote: often paired with in vivo coding

glossary.plain_definition: Verb forms ending in -ing, used as nouns.
glossary.in_this_passage: What process coding uses to name actions instead of topics.

simplifications: Presents four methods as distinct when researchers often blend them within one project.
